newsitem.title: INDIA: India warns firms not to postpone taxes to 97/98.
newsitem.headline: India warns firms not to postpone taxes to 97/98.

text.p: The Indian Finance Ministry said on Wednesday that it will take steps against companies which attempt to postpone tax payments to take advantage of proposed lower tax rates starting on April 1.
Revenue Secretary N.K. Singh has written a letter to tax officials "to ensure that advance tax which is due by the 15th of this month is paid by all major companies", it said in a statement.

In the 1997/98 (April-March) budget, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram proposed lowering corporate tax on domestic firms to 35 percent from 40 percent, and on foreign companies to 48 percent from 55 percent.
Analysts have expressed fears that some companies might try to delay the recording of income to the 1997/98 fiscal year to take advantage of the proposed lower rates.
The statement said "accounting is on an accrual basis and therefore it is not possible for corporates to postpone payments to the first quarter of the next financial year".

The ministry was keeping a close watch so ensure that the revenue targets set by the government in 1996/97 are fulfilled, said the statement, which was entitled "Governent to Take Tough Stand on Corporate Tax Postponement".
India hopes to collect 190.10 billion rupees in 1996/97 from corporate taxes and has set a target of 218.60 billion rupees in 1997/98.
